patch.value: Every instruction the product emits about its own next command is an unexecuted claim: the recovery vocabulary is generated, asserted as text, and run by nothing

The product emits a large and growing vocabulary that does not describe a result but directs the caller to a different invocation: migration_hints on the read-output receipt, restore_with on omission envelopes and omission receipts, next_steps, examples, suggested_retry and candidate_commands on refusals. Every one is a claim that something the caller wants is reachable by another spelling. Nothing executes any of them.

The class is structurally invisible to every check in place. A forward reference is emitted by one invocation and discharged by the next, so no test that captures a single invocation can observe the gap. The sentence is well formed, so schema checks pass. The flag it names exists and its value is accepted, so contract and validation checks pass. The failure surfaces only in the caller's following command, which is exactly where a coding agent operates and where no fixture looks.

First measurement, 2026-08-13, on the include dimension of the read-output contract. The hint has one generated form: '<flag> is a compatibility alias; prefer --output-include <token>.' Executed across the 18 reachable (surface, declared mode) pairs, 10 returned the requested row count with every field removed and exit 0. The hint text was asserted twice in tests/fixtures/contracts/full.json; the behaviour behind it was asserted nowhere, because every test exercising the canonical option passed field names rather than the tokens the hints recommend. The sentence was frozen by a fixture while the promise was free to not exist.

That instance is fixed and covered by tests/unit/sdk/read-output-migration-hints.spec.ts, which executes each hint rather than pinning it. This item owns the generalisation, because the include dimension is one reference kind out of at least six, and the mechanism that produced the failure is unchanged for the rest.

The population matters for sequencing. pm-0z7n exists to emit these hints at scale, and every consolidation under pm-n7rr multiplies them: seven for the list-* fold, four for history-*, more than a dozen for the annotation-facet fold. Twenty-five queued consolidations against a mechanism whose last delivery failed on 10 of 18 advertised replacements is the binding constraint on that programme, and a grammar freeze locks whichever half of a migration path is broken.

Relationship to the neighbouring work. pm-f05lsg measures whether a refusal is actionable from the refusal alone; this measures whether acting on it works, which is strictly stronger and uses the same generated-corpus machine pointed at the other half of the surface. pm-in23qu owns one instance in the candidate_commands kind, where a refusal asserted an option belongs on another path and the spelling existed on none. Neither is absorbed here.

The corpus of emitted forward references is derived from the contract tables that generate them, never hand written, and reports its own size and coverage per reference kind; Every reference asserting a replacement spelling is executed and proven to produce the same result as the spelling it replaces, excluding the receipt that records which spelling was used; Every reference asserting a recovery is executed and proven to recover, and every reference naming a command path is proven against the declared path set; The obligation set is declared as assurance data with a ratcheted pass fraction and a negative control that fails when a known-good reference is broken; Behaviour-preserving references, which explicitly retain different semantics, are separated from replacement references in the contract table and carry the weaker obligation by declaration rather than by inference
